note.question: When should a firm release complex mandatory news to attract investor attention, and do firms and investors coordinate around disclosure timing in observed markets?
note.overview: A continuum of firms chooses whether to file early or late while a representative investor simultaneously allocates scarce attention; filing and attention strategies are mutual best responses and the paper tests their equilibrium sorting predictions.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Before the filing window, firms simultaneously commit to early or late filing as a function of filing complexity and idiosyncratic timing cost, while the investor chooses aggregate attention for the two periods and distributes it across ideas. The strategies are executed in the filing window. More filings in a period dilute attention per idea and alter filer timing incentives. The EDGAR cutoff makes late processing costlier because accumulated filings appear together with less time before market open.
